chunks: Ali ibn Abdullah al-Warraq and Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Qazwini said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah ibn Abi Khalaf narrated to us, saying: Ahmad ibn Abi Khalaf al-Ash'ari narrated to us, saying: Sa'd ibn Dawud narrated to us from Malik ibn Anas, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from al-Qa'qa' ibn Hakim, from Abu Yunus, the freedman of Aisha, wife of the Prophet (peace be upon him and his Family), who said: Aisha ordered me to write for her a Mushaf (Quran codex), and she said: When you reach this verse, write: 'Maintain the prayers and the middle prayer (and the afternoon prayer), and stand before Allah devoutly,' then Aisha said: I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) by Allah.

Aisha ordered me to write for her a Mushaf, and she said: When you reach this verse, write: 'Maintain the prayers and the middle prayer (and the afternoon prayer) and stand before Allah devoutly.' Then Aisha said: I heard it from the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his Family) by Allah.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ الْوُسْطَىٰ: The middle prayer, identified here as the afternoon prayer
key_terms.مُصَحَفًا: A codex or written copy of the Quran

ai.seo_question: What is the middle prayer (Salat al-Wusta) according to Aisha's narration?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* highlights the specific identification of the 'middle prayer' as Asr, a view supported by both Shia and Sunni traditions through Aisha’s direct report. It underscores the theological emphasis on preserving the five daily prayers while granting Asr a unique status of vigilance (*qawmu lillahi qanitin*), reflecting the practical and spiritual discipline central to Islamic worship.
